messages:
alex_customer: Hey team — hitting a nasty bug when we fan out multiple tool calls in parallel. Some tool_result objects are being associated with the wrong tool id. We see schema validation 400s for tool B even though the payload clearly matches its schema. Correlation id: coro:0a1b2c3d. Example request (simplified):
```json
{
  "input": "summarize docs",
  "tools": [
    {"id": "tool_a", "args": {"doc_id": 123}},
    {"id": "tool_b", "args": {"query": "top_k=5"}}
  ]
}
```
We send both concurrently (parallel:true) and sometimes the response payload for tool_a ends up under tool_b in the response array. This causes downstream parsing to fail and we get unexpected charges. Any known issues?

jess_support: Sorry about that, Alex. Can you paste the full response body (redact PII) and the request id from the API response headers? Also which SDK + version?

alex_customer: Request header x-request-id: xrq-9f8e7d. SDK: node redwood@2.3.1. Sample (redacted):
```json
{
  "request_id": "xrq-9f8e7d",
  "tools_results": [
    {"tool_id": "tool_a", "result": {"summary": "..."}},
    {"tool_id": "tool_b", "error": {"code": 400, "message": "schema validation failed: missing field 'query'"}}
  ]
}
```
But logs show tool_b got the right args.

jess_support: Thanks. I'm escalating to runtime and ML infra. @tyler_eng-runtime, can you take a look at fanout/association logic? Seems like parallel-output association might be racy.

tyler_eng-runtime: digging in. Do you have a full trace id or span? coro:0a1b2c3d you mentioned — can you attach the API gateway logs showing routing decisions?

alex_customer: Pushed the gateway logs to the shared S3 link: s3://redwood-support-uploads/xrq-9f8e7d-gateway.log. Also attached a small repro script that parallels two axios calls to /v1/invoke with the same parent id.

priya_eng-ml: I suspect the tool selection/choice layer's temp cache might be reusing a mutable object when calls are parallelized. We had a similar bug 6 months ago fixed for sequenced calls. If the tool_result array is constructed using shared pointers and ordering relies on insertion order without stable ids, interleaving can occur.

marta_oncall: Created incident INC-2024-1234 for visibility and paging. @oncall please monitor latency spikes — customers report increased 500s when this happens.

ops_bot: Incident INC-2024-1234 created by marta_oncall. Severity: P2. Pager duty escalation sent.

tyler_eng-runtime: Found a suspicious race in async reduce that builds the results array: when Promise.all resolves, we map results back using an incremental index rather than the tool_id. If two parallel tool invocations complete out of order and the mapping uses positional indices tied to request arrival rather than tool_id, association flips. Patch in progress.

omar_billing: FYI — we have 4 disputed charges from this customer referencing xrq-9f8e7d for duplicate tool executions. Hold billing until we confirm root cause. Alex, can you confirm which charges you see?

alex_customer: I see charges: ch_1A2B, ch_1A2C (same timestamp). Yes please hold. These are nontrivial.

jess_support: Workaround for now: please set parallel:false or serialize calls as a temporary fix. That should keep mapping stable. Tyler, can we get a hotfix?

tyler_eng-runtime: Yes — prepping a patch to map by explicit tool_id at result assembly and add defensive checks (verify tool_id in response matches requested id), will ship hotfix to canary in next 30m and rollback if errors.

priya_eng-ml: Also adding unit tests that simulate high concurrency with randomized completion order to prevent regressions.

marta_oncall: Noted. I'll update the customer-facing status page once hotfix is live.

jess_support: Alex — thanks for the detailed repro. We'll keep you updated in this thread. For immediate relief, set parallel:false and we'll refund duplicate charges after root cause confirmed. 

alex_customer: Thanks — switched to serial and problem stopped. Appreciate the quick triage. :thumbsup:
